title: A declining background breaks the inverse-rate duration rule in a constant-normal-stress rate-state model
abstract: An Oklahoma study found a clustering taper proportional to background rate to the power -0.25, rather than -1. We test the steady-background assumption in that comparison. In a constant-normal-stress rate-state population model, we derive an exact paired response to a stress step. Its relative memory decays with cumulative unperturbed earthquake count. A declining background adds to absolute rate decay. A constructed finite-window response gives an exponent of 0.236 with fixed friction parameters, although its steady-background limit gives 1. A two-parameter response curve describes five published aggregate tapers with log RMS error 0.092, against 0.164 for a power curve. This is a descriptive comparison, not a catalog likelihood test. The example requires unloading in its lower-rate groups. We give an exact count-clock diagnostic, a loading-sign test, and 12 independent ODE checks. The result shows why the exponent alone cannot establish nonlinear stressing-rate sensitivity. It does not identify the residual Oklahoma driver, estimate a field stress history, or improve a forecast. Normal-stress changes, heterogeneous fault populations, and earthquake feedback remain outside the tested model.

display.caption: Exact population responses and a descriptive comparison with five published free ETAS tapers. The response time is a finite-window log slope, not a fitted ETAS taper.
A stress step has a straight-line response in cumulative unperturbed count under the tested assumptions. These lines are model predictions, not catalog measurements.
